title: Digital Transformation and the Adoption of Strategic Management Accounting Among Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises in Soweto, South Africa: A Literature Review
content: The rapid advancement of digital technologies has transformed the operational and strategic landscape of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs), creating opportunities to improve organisational performance through digitally enabled Strategic Management Accounting (SMA). While traditional management accounting primarily supports operational control and historical financial reporting, SMA extends this role by integrating financial and non-financial information to facilitate strategic planning, competitive positioning, and long-term decision-making. The emergence of cloud computing, artificial intelligence, enterprise resource planning systems, big data analytics, blockchain, and mobile accounting has significantly enhanced the ability of SMEs to generate timely, accurate, and strategic information. Despite these opportunities, the adoption of digitally enabled SMA remains uneven, particularly among township-based SMEs operating in resource-constrained environments such as Soweto, South Africa. Existing literature indicates that organisational limitations, technological barriers, infrastructural deficiencies, regulatory uncertainty, and inadequate managerial capabilities continue to constrain digital transformation within SMEs. Furthermore, much of the existing research has focused on large organisations and developed economies, resulting in limited understanding of how digital transformation influences SMA adoption within township businesses. This literature review critically synthesises current scholarly evidence regarding Strategic Management Accounting, digital transformation, theoretical explanations for technology adoption, and the organisational factors influencing digitally enabled SMA implementation among SMEs. The review further identifies major research gaps and proposes future research directions that contribute to both theory and practice by providing a context-specific understanding of digital transformation and strategic accounting within South African township economies.
